info.title: Stowage Management
info.description: Inventory manager for Signal K Server: organize items into containers and storage spaces, track actual vs. target quantities, attach photos and markdown notes, and map storage spaces to areas on an SVG floorplan.

tags.description: Storage spaces and containers (a shared hierarchy)

post.summary: Create a storage space or container

parent_id.description: Parent location id. Required for containers to nest inside something (omit for a top-level storage space).

400.description: Missing/invalid name or type, or parent_id does not exist

delete.description: Only succeeds if the location has no child locations and no items directly in it.

patch.description: Moves a container under another container or storage space, or makes a location top-level by omitting/nulling parent_id. Rejects moves that would create a cycle.

400.description: parent_id does not exist, is the location itself, or would create a cycle

patch.summary: Assign or clear a storage space's floorplan area
patch.description: Only valid on locations of type storage_space. Pass null/omit both fields to clear the mapping.

svg_element_id.description: The id attribute of the SVG shape representing this storage space.

400.description: Not a storage_space, or floorplan_id does not exist

200.description: All items, each with a categories array

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match against item name only (not notes). Returns all matches, unbounded.

note.description: Optional note recorded in the item log for the initial quantity.

400.description: Missing name, or location_id/category_id does not exist

patch.description: Partial update. target_quantity and notes support an explicit null to clear them, distinct from omitting the key (which leaves the current value unchanged). If the item is split across locations, actual_quantity cannot be set here — use POST /items/:id/split instead; name/notes/target_quantity remain editable normally.

note.description: Optional note recorded in the item log if actual_quantity and/or target_quantity change in this request.

default_location_id.description: Only settable on a split item, and only to a location_id matching one of its current placements (400 otherwise). Null clears it.

patch.summary: Set or clear an item's photo

thumbnail.description: A data: URI (e.g. a JPEG data URI), or null/omitted to remove the thumbnail.

patch.summary: Move an item to a different location

location_id.description: Omit/null to unassign the item (no location).

patch.description: Moves a whole (unsplit) item to a different location. Rejected with 400 if the item is currently split across locations — move a specific placement via PATCH /items/:id/placements/:placementId/move instead.

post.summary: Add a category to an item

delete.summary: Remove a category from an item

get.summary: Find the mapped storage space for an item
get.description: Walks up the item's location chain until it finds a storage space mapped to a floorplan area, so a client knows which SVG element to highlight. Works no matter how deeply the item is nested in containers.

200.description: A mapped storage space was found

404.description: Item has no location, or no mapped storage space was found in its location chain

409.description: A category with this name already exists
A category with this name already exists

delete.description: Also removes this category from every item that had it.

get.description: Returns id/name/uploaded_at only (not the SVG content); ordered newest first.

400.description: Missing name/svg_content, or svg_content is not valid SVG

get.summary: Get one floorplan including its SVG content

delete.description: Only succeeds if no storage space is still mapped to it.

400.description: Floorplan is still mapped to storage spaces

get.description: Returns raw log rows for item creation, actual/target quantity changes, and deletion (item moves are not logged). Optionally filtered to a date range; start/end are inclusive date strings (e.g. 2026-06-01).
Empty array means the item is not split.

patch.summary: Move one placement of a split item
patch.description: Not logged, same as an ordinary item move.

post.summary: Split an item's stock across locations
post.description: Moves `quantity` units from from_location_id to to_location_id, splitting the item across locations if it wasn't already split. from/to may be omitted/null for "no location". If the item wasn't split yet, from_location_id must match its current location_id. If splitting collapses the item back down to a single location (e.g. moving everything back together), it automatically reverts to the plain (unsplit) representation. Always logged as a 'split' event, regardless of the resulting state.

200.description: Updated item, including its new placements array

400.description: Invalid quantity, same from/to, location doesn't exist, from_location_id doesn't match where the item currently is, or insufficient quantity at from_location_id

patch.description: The split-item equivalent of PATCH /items/:id { actual_quantity }. The item's overall actual_quantity is kept in sync (it's always the sum of its placements) and the change is logged as an ordinary 'actual_quantity' event, exactly like editing a normal item's quantity — this is a real stock change, not a reallocation between locations, so it is deliberately not a 'split' event. Setting a placement to 0 removes it; if that leaves only one placement, the item automatically reverts to the plain (unsplit) representation.

200.description: Updated item, including its new placements array

400.description: quantity is not a non-negative integer

post.summary: Upload an attachment for an item
post.description: The request body is the raw file bytes (not JSON) — there's no size limit and no file-type restriction, and files are stored on disk rather than in the database. Set Content-Type to the file's MIME type, and pass the original filename URI-encoded in the X-Filename header.

get.description: Serves the raw file with its original Content-Type and Content-Disposition, so the browser renders it natively (PDFs/images inline, everything else downloads).

Categories, locations (with hierarchy and floorplan mappings), and items (with their categories, placements, and attachment metadata). Excludes floorplan SVG content, attachment file contents, and Store Log history.

post.summary: Restore from a full inventory snapshot
post.description: Restores or merges a snapshot (same shape GET /export returns), controlled by the payload's optional `mode` field (default "replace"). `mode: "replace"` replaces categories/locations/items entirely with the given snapshot (a restore, not a merge). `mode: "merge"` (#26) instead adds the snapshot's rows alongside what's already there: an id from the payload is kept unless it collides with an existing row, in which case a new one is generated and every reference to it (item.location_id, item.category_ids, placement.location_id, location.parent_id) is remapped to match; a category is matched to an existing one by exact name and merged into it rather than duplicated; a location name colliding with an existing sibling under the same parent is disambiguated with a " (2)", " (3)", ... suffix; and a parent_id/location_id may reference a row already in the target database instead of one included in the payload, for importing new items/locations into an existing tree. In both modes: floorplans (including any in the snapshot) are never created or modified by import, nor are attachment files or Store Log history; a location's floorplan mapping only survives if that floorplan_id (or, failing that, a floorplan with matching svg_content) exists in the target database, otherwise it's dropped and counted in dropped_floorplan_mappings.

categories_matched_existing.description: merge mode only: imported categories matched to an existing one by name instead of being created.

locations_renamed.description: merge mode only: imported locations renamed with a " (2)", " (3)", ... suffix to avoid a name clash with an existing sibling.

get.summary: Get plugin-level webapp config: theme automation and quantity-step scaling
get.description: Reflects two plugin options (set in the SignalK Admin UI's Plugin Config page): 'Automatically switch light/dark theme based on sun position' (autoTheme, plus the currently recommended theme based on vessels.self.environment.sun/mode when it's on), and 'Dynamic +/- scale for touch interface' (dynamicQuantityScale). Named /webapp-config rather than /config to avoid colliding with signalk-server's own reserved GET /plugins/{id}/config endpoint (which returns the plugin's enabled/configuration metadata, not this).

placements.description: Empty for a normal item. Non-empty means this item's stock is split across multiple locations — in that case actual_quantity is the sum of placement quantities, location_id is null, and actual_quantity can only be changed via POST /items/:id/split.

expires_at.description: Optional expiration date (YYYY-MM-DD). Not tracked in the item log.

default_location_id.description: Only meaningful for a split item; must match one of its current item_placements' location_id. The quick +/- quantity editors (Overview, Categories, the Touch view) act on this placement's quantity when set. Cleared automatically if that placement is drained, moved elsewhere, or the item collapses back to a single location.

acquired_date.description: Optional date this item was acquired (YYYY-MM-DD).

price_paid.description: Optional price paid for this item, no currency tracked.

item_id.description: Not a foreign key — the row survives item deletion

item_name.description: Snapshotted at the time of the event, so history reads correctly after renames

mode.description: Import-only, ignored by /export. Defaults to "replace" (full restore) when omitted; "merge" adds the payload's rows alongside existing data instead. See POST /import's description.
